fit_models.scope: The scheme brackets conjugate formation and subsequent processing as one observed phase. k_app_max belongs to that saturated multistep phase, not either individual arrow. The source interprets K_0.5 within a cooperative preceding-binding model; no model-independent affinity is assigned. The equation retains the source Hill exponent n; its numeric coefficient remains in the unchanged original provider and is not projected through this model link.

deposit_absence_reason: No matching MAP-bound arrangement or assay-construct-to-deposit relation is established by the selected retained evidence. Data Availability names 6HAF as L. plantarum E59Q in complex with phosphate: both construct and ligand differ from these wild-type MAP/pyruvate contexts. No geometry, atom map or physical preparation identity is substituted. The retained Figure7a legend names 4FEG as wild-type POX with a carbanion-enamine Breslow intermediate, but no retained 4FEG coordinates/arrangement or assay-preparation identity supports a model association here.

discriminant.finding: MAP kon/koff describe reversible apparent binding including its covalent conjugate. Pyruvate k_app_max describes the saturated FAD-reduction phase across conjugate formation and subsequent processing; neither individual pyruvate phase arrow has an assigned rate here.
discriminant.consequential_exclusion: Do not assign MAP parameters to pyruvate, compare kon directly with first-order rates, or use k_app_max as an individual conjugate-formation or decarboxylation rate. K_D_app and K_0.5 retain different ligand/model roles.
discriminant.positive_content: One consumer recovers source-labelled state paths, fit coverage and five exact existing endpoints with their original assays.
discriminant.first_missing_premise: No atom-resolved microstates or matching MAP structural arrangement is established; source Eox-S and P labels do not supply a complete reacted-state mechanism.

limitations: A source kinetic scheme is not an atom-mapped elementary mechanism, trajectory, productive design template or laboratory result of this project.
The FAD-reduction endpoint supplies no individual microscopic rate or oxygen-turnover kinetic constant. DCPIP steady-state observations remain separate and unchanged.
MAP is not further processed in the reported assay; its stable C-P bond explanation stays source-attributed. No zero downstream rate is created.
Wild-type scheme association does not establish a MAP conjugate for E59Q. Its source-reported nonbinding and unavailable values remain unchanged.
The original assays retain 25 C, pH 6.0 for MAP and unspecified pH for single turnover, optical path-length typo, table triplicate SD and separate Figure8 repeat statement.

Exact sequences, assay specimens, atomic protonation/tautomerism and physical preparation identity remain unresolved. Full main text and Extended Data Figure8 images were not newly acquired; retained SI, table and accessible legends supply this annotation.

acquisition.redistribution_scope: The four reused publisher bodies are not redistributed. The previously tracked RCSB 6HA3 coordinate file remains redistributed and unchanged.

reconsideration.bespoke_chemistry_code: Shared optional-arrangement and source-fit relations extend model_links; ligand, source states and parameter roles live in data. No enzyme-ID branch.
reconsideration.reuse: Second enzyme context uses existing provider values and consumer; no new numeric transcriptions, duplicate primary witnesses or observed time-saving claim. Model meaning and source selection still require curation.
reconsideration.integrated_value: Fit coverage prevents a multistep apparent reporter parameter from becoming an individual transition rate. The ligand branches prevent MAP-to-pyruvate transfer. A competent reader can derive these distinctions from the source; no incumbent superiority or complete atlas is claimed.
